text:
jordan: Heads up — noticed rack12-host43 PCIe errors ramping over the last 30m, correlating with a tail-latency bump for several multi-tenant slices. logs attached from the node below. thinking we should put a soft-cordon on that host (no new allocations) and carve temporary cushion slices for tier-1 tenants while we investigate. thoughts?

infra-bot: ALERT: pcie_crc_errors > threshold on rack12-host43 (host43.rack12.redwood.internal). metric spike started 2026-03-21T09:02Z.

maria: thanks for flagging. can you paste the prometheus query and sample output? want to see if it's sustained or bursty. also which tenants are affected?

jordan: query: `increase(node_pcie_crc_errors_total{host="host43"}[15m])` -> 42 in last 15m. tail p99 for affected slices up ~120ms from baseline. affected tenants: finance-ingest (heavy batching), ad-campaign-sim (bursty), and a couple of small dev teams.

kevin: 42 in 15m is not tiny. could be gradual hardware degradation (cable/slot) or a driver microcode mismatch. any recent driver/firmware rollouts to that rack?

jordan: no infra rollout in last 48h. last firmware update was two weeks ago.

jen-sre: from SRE POV I'd prefer a soft-cordon first (prevent new placements) + migrate high-SLA jobs to a warm dedicated slice in us-west-2-edge while we triage. migration window target: next rolling maintenance slot (in ~2h) unless evict pressure is high.

chris: +1 for soft-cordon. for the cushion: we have 2 spare A100 slots in us-west-2-edge warm pool that are underutilized. we can carve 1-2 temporary reserved pods for the impacted tenants. need cost signal — is this charged to infra or product?

maria: we'll need to invoice properly. Product wants to avoid surprise credits. proposal: infra cover migration infra cost for now and product will decide crediting after postmortem. also we should track per-tenant latency/regression for chargeback.

kevin: quick triage steps: 1) soft-cordon host43 2) force-graceful drain of non-critical preemptible pods (`kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60 host/host43`) 3) move tier-1 stateful slices to dedicated warm nodes 4) run `lspci -vvv` and capture CRC counters + `dmesg` for ECC messages.

jordan: doing step 1 now. executing: `./infractl cordon host43 --soft`

infra-bot: ACTION: cordon requested by jordan on host43. status: soft-cordon in effect — new placements halted.

jordan: starting a graceful drain for best-effort preemptible jobs. will avoid killing reserved tenant jobs. paste of `kubectl get pods --field-selector spec.nodeName=host43` shows ~27 pods, ~10 preemptible.

jen-sre: for migration automation, can we use the existing warm-pool-swap playbook? (it's been used once for AZ warmup). need to ensure affinity rules keep the financial tenant away from preemptible pools.

chris: yes we can. I'll start the playbook for finance-ingest and ad-campaign-sim. ETA ~12 minutes.

maria: ops question — when we carve temporary dedicated slices, should we enable egress QoS to protect against noisy-tenant egress hogs? last time ad-campaign-sim saturated NVLink -> cross-host perf hit.

kevin: enable per-tenant egress shaper at 90th percentile observed load + small burst buffer. also enforce NVLink isolation tag on the reserved slices.

jordan: log snippet from host43 dmesg (tail):
```
Mar 21 09:05:12 host43 kernel: pcieport 0000:3c:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=00e0
Mar 21 09:05:12 host43 kernel: pcieport 0000:3c:00.0: AER: PCIe Bus Error: severity=Corrected, type=Data Link, id=00e0
Mar 21 09:07:03 host43 kernel: nvidia: GPU 0: ECC single-bit error, address=0x7f9a... count=1
```

jen-sre: that looks like intermittent link-level corrections; could be a marginal cable or retimers. Ops should test a NIC/retimer swap if host maintenance window allows. If not, continue soft-cordon and migration.

chris: playbook completed for finance-ingest -> reserved-node-uw2-edge-02. ad-campaign-sim queued. monitoring migration impact now.

maria: product finance notified. initiated cost hold and will review credit policy post incident. tracking ticket: PLAT-4231.

kevin: parallel step: run `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,SM,PCI` and collect GPU telemetry. send to hw-eng. also open a hardware RMA request if counters continue to rise.

jordan: ran `nvidia-smi` — no current ECC fatal, single-bit count matches dmesg. uploading output to S3: https://s3.redwood.internal/logs/host43/pci-ecc-20260321.log

infra-bot: MONITOR: pcie_crc_errors decreased after cordon+drain but still averaging ~4/15m. will re-evaluate in 30m.

jen-sre: if counts continue to persist, schedule block maintenance for rack12 1am-3am window. for now, let the soft-cordon hold and watch.

maria: action items captured: jordan — continue monitoring and attach metrics to PLAT-4231; chris — confirm warm pool reservation sticky; kevin — collect GPU/PCIe telemetry + open RMA if needed; jen-sre — sign off on maintenance window if persisted.

jordan: noted. will update thread with 30m snapshot. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
